title: Ops-centric feedback rollup and proposals
content:
Objective:

This note consolidates operator-facing customer feedback gathered from Aug 2026 support threads, CSM interviews, and field calls (5 large customers). The goal is to translate recurring operational pain points into a short prioritized list of concrete product/UX fixes and engineering proposals that reduce toil and reduce incidents related to Dedicated/Private inference.

Collection & signals used:
- Support tickets flagged as "ops-impact" (CS-4100..CS-4140) from 2026-08
- 1:1 interviews with SRE leads at three customers (enterprise search, agent platform, embedded assistant)
- Field notes from solutions engineering run during two on-prem installations
- Console logs & traces reviewed for highest-severity incidents in Aug

High-level synthesis (operator lens):
- Theme A: Observability gaps that make incident triage slow. Common ask: per-request KV-cache hit rate, per-model 99th pct token latency, and token-cost breakouts for failed vs succeeded responses.
- Theme B: Failure handling and graceful degradation needs. Customers want rule-based fallbacks (route to cheaper quantized model, degrade to short responses) that are configurable at routing layer and visible in console.
- Theme C: Autoscale & burst policies for Dedicated are underpowered for spiky agent workloads; customers want predictable burst ceilings and simulated impact before committing to reserved capacity.
- Theme D: Private deployment onboarding friction: network/KMS checks, expected firewall rules, and a preflight checklist are requested.
- Theme E: Documentation and runbooks exist but are out of sync with current runtime behavior (e.g., cache invalidation signals changed in v0.9.3).

Representative customer quotes (anonymized):
- "When latency jumps we spend >2 hours just finding which model and prefix caused the KV miss. We need better signals at the request level." (Large search infra customer)
- "We'd like a knob to say: if the dedicated pool is saturated, route to a 'fallback' variant rather than hard 429s. Right now our app suffers in production during traffic spikes." (SaaS platform)
- "Private deployment onboarding took 4 full-days to get KMS & firewall rules right — we expected a 1-day setup." (Financial customer)

Prioritized ask list (ops impact x customer frequency) — quick view:
1) Expose per-request analytics in Console (token-level cost + KV hit/miss + model variant) — Impact: high, Frequency: very high, Effort: S-M
2) Routing fallback policies (configurable by route/model: degrade/route/queue) + console visualization — Impact: high, Frequency: high, Effort: M-L
3) Dedicated burst simulator (tool: simulate N qps and show tail latency & projected spend) — Impact: medium-high, Frequency: medium, Effort: M
4) Private preflight & network/KMS checklist + onboarding runbook update (package of docs + automated preflight check script) — Impact: high for new deploys, Frequency: medium, Effort: S
5) KV cache observability: per-pool and per-prefix metrics + alert templates — Impact: medium, Frequency: high, Effort: S-M
6) Update runbooks & incident playbooks to reflect runtime v0.9.x changes (including cache invalidation and batching fallback behavior) — Impact: medium, Frequency: medium, Effort: S

Examples / short proposals for each item:
1) Per-request analytics
- Add an option to persist a lightweight request footprint that surfaces: model-id, model-variant, tokens-in/out, kv-hit-flag, queue-time, and per-request cost estimate. Default: off; enable via project setting for retention 7 days.
- Console: searchable table + deep-link to trace.
- Quick win: expose via existing tracing link (no new storage) for last 7 days; later add aggregated UI.

2) Routing fallback policies
- Policy API: {primary_model, fallbacks:[{model, criteria}], behavior: {route|truncate|queue}}.
- Start with server-side config for Hosted/Dedicated; Private can use same API via control plane sync.
- UX: a rules editor with simulation showing where requests would route.

3) Dedicated burst simulator
- Small web tool where customers input QPS distribution (or upload sample trace) and we run a sandboxed sizing simulation that replays batching & scheduling logic to estimate tail latency and spend.
- Use for sales conversations and during Dedicated onboarding.

4) Private preflight 
- Create a small CLI script that checks: KMS connectivity, required ports, NTP sync, docker/gpu driver versions, and returns a pass/fail + guidance.
- Document firewall rules in a single checklist PDF for customers and Solutions Engineers.

5) KV cache observability
- Emit metrics: kv_total_lookups, kv_hits, kv_miss_by_prefix, kv_evictions, kv_latency_ms (per pool).
- Provide alert templates (e.g., kv_miss_rate>10% sustained 5m -> page oncall).

6) Runbook updates
- One-pager change notes for runtime team to publish breaking behavior changes and suggested pager actions (e.g., when to scale dedicated pool, when to route to fallback).

Open questions & unknowns:
- Privacy: storing per-request footprints creates a small PII/exposure risk for customers (prompts may be included). Need to define an opt-in model and scrub sensitive content.
- Resource cost: how much storage & query cost will per-request capture add to Console? Estimate needed.
- Fallback semantics across streaming & function-calling flows — subtle behavior differences to enumerate.

Suggested quick wins (<=2w):
- Publish private deployment preflight checklist and a short "what to expect" onboarding doc (SE-run).
- Create an alert template for kv_miss_rate and a sample Dashboard tile that SEs can paste into customer consoles.
- Add a small section in the Console describing current fallback behaviors and where to find the routing rules (docs).

Medium-term work (4–10w):
- Build routing fallback policy API + console editor prototype, gated behind feature flag.
- Implement kv cache metrics emission + integrate with existing dashboards.

Longer term (>10w):
- Per-request analytics with safe-mode scrubbing and retention controls; UI for analysis and rollup.
- Dedicated burst simulator integrated into sales/console flows.

Ownership & next steps:
- CS to own short-term docs + alert templates (Priya, Lena) — target: 2026-10-08 to publish artifacts and inform the SE team.
- Runtime/Serving to triage feasibility of per-request footprint (ENG owner: Marcos Alvarez to kick off RFC) — target RFC by 2026-10-15.
- Product to prototype routing policy UX (owner: Ethan Cole) — exploratory wireframes due 2026-10-20.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Follow up with security on data retention/privacy model for request footprint (Sofia to ping security)
- Add sample customer trace (anonymized) to linked artifacts for sim work
- Run quick poll on SE slack to validate demand for burst simulator (copy of this doc + 2 question survey)

Unresolved items to surface in review:
- Confirmation on whether private deployments can accept policy syncs from control plane by default.
- Budget estimate for storing per-request footprints vs. offering ephemeral traces only.

-- End of rollup --

(Informal: this doc is intentionally ops-focused — aim is to make incidents faster to resolve and reduce repeat escalations. Reviews welcome: add comments inline or ping me in #cs-product channel.)
